title: Top Three Earners
statement:
Find the three highest paid employees.

The `employees` table has one row per employee:

- `id`: the employee's id, unique
- `name`: the employee's full name, unique
- `department`: the team they work in
- `salary`: their yearly salary in whole dollars

Return the `name` and `salary` of the three employees with the highest salaries, highest first. When two salaries are equal, the name that comes first alphabetically goes first, and that also decides who makes the cut for third place. When there are fewer than three employees, return all of them.

Expected output:

```text
    name    | salary
------------+--------
 Priya Nair |  98000
 Aisha Khan |  91000
 Elena Ruiz |  87000
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE employees (
  id integer PRIMARY KEY,
  name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  department text NOT NULL,
  salary integer NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES
  (1, 'Priya Nair', 'Engineering', 98000),
  (2, 'Marcus Bell', 'Sales', 87000),
  (3, 'Elena Ruiz', 'Engineering', 87000),
  (4, 'Tom Becker', 'Support', 72000),
  (5, 'Aisha Khan', 'Design', 91000),
  (6, 'Leo Park', 'Support', 65000),
  (7, 'Hannah Cole', 'Marketing', 79000),
  (8, 'Omar Haddad', 'Sales', 58000);

tests.output:
name    | salary
------------+--------
 Priya Nair |  98000
 Aisha Khan |  91000
 Elena Ruiz |  87000
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES (9, 'Zoe Adams', 'Engineering', 120000);
tests.output:
name    | salary
------------+--------
 Zoe Adams  | 120000
 Priya Nair |  98000
 Aisha Khan |  91000
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: UPDATE employees SET salary = 87000 WHERE name = 'Priya Nair';
tests.output:
name     | salary
-------------+--------
 Aisha Khan  |  91000
 Elena Ruiz  |  87000
 Marcus Bell |  87000
(3 rows)

tests.stdin:
DELETE FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000;
INSERT INTO employees (id, name, department, salary) VALUES (9, 'Bruno Silva', 'Design', 72000);
tests.output:
name     | salary
-------------+--------
 Hannah Cole |  79000
 Bruno Silva |  72000
 Tom Becker  |  72000
(3 rows)

name    | salary
------------+--------
 Priya Nair |  98000
 Aisha Khan |  91000
(2 rows)

hints: `ORDER BY` takes several columns, separated by commas. The second one only matters when the first one ties.
Add `DESC` to sort a column from highest to lowest, then keep the first rows with `LIMIT`.

sql.solution:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC, name
LIMIT 3;
